posts.title: The UK’s major events and festivals need a government that “joins up across departments and removes barriers”, say MPs
posts.description: The UK’s standing as a “global leader” when it comes to hosting major events, including large-scale music events and festivals, should not be taken for granted, according to a new report by MPs, who note that event organisers are facing “intensifying competition from abroad, rising operating costs and an increasingly complex regulatory environment”. The government has a role to play in helping event organisers navigate these challenges, according to Parliament’s Digital, Culture, Media & Sport Select Committee , and that begins with better coordination between, and clearer access to, relevant government departments, as well as “a more strategic approach to growth”. According to Committee Chair Caroline Dinenage MP , given the “clear cultural and economic significance” of major cultural and sporting events in the UK, “it’s a travesty that major events do not receive enough recognition or support from across government”. posts.title: CMU Selects - the last week’s standout releases
posts.description: Louis Ottley’s new single ‘Jeffrey's Son’ Drum and bass with MC flow, but make no mistake, this is punk music. Unrelenting, until it cracks open and a synth melody climbs through, changing the temperature entirely. Ray Laurél’s new album ‘ Neptune Rising ’ Ray Laurél is a Gen Z Prince and this album furthers the case - crunchy guitars, looping synths, vocals that treat desire like a force of nature. Friedberg’s new single ‘Mitsubishi’ Acid-tinged, DAF-adjacent dance-punk that also might just be a song about driving a car. This track started life as a Krautrock demo - then drummer Fifi Dewey sped it up, dropped in a hard bassline, and recorded live drums and a lot of cowbells in Walthamstow. From the band’s second album ‘Goodwife’, out in April. Novelist’s new album ‘SCENES’ Eight years between albums, but Novelist has spent that time well. 25 tracks cutting through grime, 80s soul, baile funk and jungle, with spoken-word skits on everything from raves to aliens holding it together. posts.title: Judge declines to dismiss Suno publicity rights case, as sixteen more musicians join the legal battle
posts.description: A US judge has declined to dismiss the lawsuit led by singer-songwriter Jason Isbell which accuses Suno of infringing the publicity rights of artists. Judge Angel Kelley denied Suno’s motion to dismiss Isbell’s lawsuit yesterday following the submission of an amended complaint by the musician’s legal team on Tuesday. Indeed, Kelley said Suno’s motion to dismiss was denied “in light of the amended complaint”. This is the Suno lawsuit that stands out from all the others because it centres on publicity rights rather than copyright, accusing the AI company of infringing the publicity rights of artists by “indexing musicians by name”, so that it can generate new music “in the style” of existing artists, exploiting each musician’s “identifying attributes”.
